tanya (runtime): Heads-up: ran a targeted probe against mi250 nightly images. Kernel lookup is missing for a narrow seqlen band (~1024) and we see 2.5-3x tail latency on short-chat traces. Logs + perf snippets below.

kevin: thanks — can you paste the lookup snippet? is this kv cache related or purely kernel inventory?

tanya (runtime): here's a trimmed log from the lookup path:```
[2024-05-15T03:12:34Z] kernel_lookup: model=gpt-3b op=matmul arch=mi250 seq_len=1024 -> kernel_id=NONE fallback=generic_tiled reason="no_matching_tiling" routing_policy=conditional_autoroute batching_bucket=short
[2024-05-15T03:12:34Z] autotuner: candidate mi250-int8-tiling-1024 -> result=REJECTED check=nan_tolerance mismatch=3e-8
[2024-05-15T03:12:34Z] router: selected fallback kernel=generic_tiled latency_est=35ms measured=78ms
```

anil: saw a similar pattern in yesterday's microbench reports — autotuner rejected several mi250 tilings at larger seqlens because numeric diffs were marginal. Did the autotuner threshold change?

tanya (runtime): autotuner job logs show it tightened correctness epsilon in last deploy, yes. It flagged one tiling as flaky (nan compare failure). Because the inventory had no "nearest" candidate for seq=1024, router fell back to generic_tiled which is much slower on MI250.

sam (perf): what about KV cache? If KV hits are high we prefer small-block kernels. Are these traces where prefix is served from kv cache then a new chunk pushes seq into 1024?

tanya (runtime): KV hits for these traces are ~82%. The race is: initial request uses cached KV prefix so we estimate seq bucket low, but when we materialize the live prefix (some missing frames) seq snaps to ~1024 and we run a fresh kernel lookup. The lookup runs after the batch estimator already bucketed the batch, so we get a mismatch and no candidate found.

ops-bot: Incident INF-2026-019 created: https://infra.redwood/internal/INF-2026-019 Assigned: kevin, anil

kevin: short-term mitigation plan: if kernel_lookup returns none for mi250 and seqlen in [900,1100], force-select the nearest tile candidate (best-effort) instead of generic_tiled and emit metric kernel_lookup.soft_route=1. I'll land canary tonight.

anil: ok for a quick fix. long-term: autotuner needs a retry with relaxed correctness (or a rebaseline) for mi250 tilings in that band and a microbench against production traces. Also consider preserving a shadow inventory of "approximate" kernels for conditional routing.

tanya (runtime): another contributing factor — the batching heuristic: when batch size > 8 we currently squash and set seq_len=max across batch. That makes the lookup more likely to hit the 1024 bucket and discover missing tilings. We should clamp the estimator or run per-req lookup before batching for seqlen-sensitive models.

sam (perf): please capture a rocprof sample and the autotuner stdout for a failing candidate. I'll run an isolated perf job with the same inputs. Also add a microbenchmark that toggles cache prefix length mid-request.

tanya (runtime): uploaded gist with perf hist + autotuner logs: https://redwood-gists/mi250-1024-probe (contains rocprof sample, autotuner stdout, tracer).

kevin: :thumbsup: I'll push the soft-route canary + metrics: kernel_lookup.misses, fallback.type, seqlen_bucket, autotune.reject_reason. Will also log batch_estimator.size at lookup-time.

anil: add a CI test that marks autotune candidates as FLAKY instead of REJECTED when numeric diffs are within a slack window, then schedule a re-run job against prod traces. We lost coverage by being too strict.

tanya (runtime): PR draft: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/1234 — includes: soft-route for mi250 band, metric instrumentation, and a small batch estimator clamp. Will test on canary.

sam (perf): reminder: validate KV cache interplay end-to-end. Add a psych test that toggles prefix length mid-batch and asserts no kernel lookup mismatch.

kevin: noted. I'll report canary metrics in #releases after the midnight deploy.

tanya (runtime): TL;DR root cause = (1) stricter autotune correctness rejected valid-but-noisy tilings, (2) batching estimator amplifies seqlen bucketing, (3) KV cache/lookup race pushes some requests into an uncovered seqlen path. Immediate plan = soft-route + telemetry, autotune re-run with relaxed thresholds, CI tests for prefix toggle. Updating INF ticket with timeline.

kevin: thanks — assign me for canary and metrics. Ping if the canary shows regression.

anil: I'll own the autotune job and flaky-mark change.

tanya (runtime): will follow up with canary logs and perf dash in the incident. Thanks all.
